limitations: The >20% and 5.5–10% results are passive AC-to-AC efficiencies; approximately 5% is an end-to-end DC-to-DC prototype metric.
The AC-to-AC and DC-to-DC measurements do not necessarily share the same position, power or impedance-tuning point.

At the 500 mW condition, the paper reports simulated SAR below basic restrictions in a simplified cylindrical phantom, while external magnetic reference levels can be locally exceeded near the relay. This is not blanket compliance certification.
Multiple active relays redistribute power and can reduce per-node delivery; the paper advocates selective or time-multiplexed activation rather than a universal fixed capacity.

claim_audit.claim_text: Hierarchical link improves power transfer efficiency by more than two orders of magnitude relative to direct room-scale transfer.
claim_audit.notes: The cited Fig.2d example reports >20% relay-assisted AC-to-AC efficiency versus approximately 0.3% direct baseline. That specific contrast is >66x; the abstract's >100x claim refers to the broader set of results/conditions, not one universal gain.

claim_audit.claim_text: At the 500 mW operating condition, modelled SAR remained below ICNIRP general-public basic restrictions despite local external-field reference-level exceedance.
claim_audit.notes: Simulated with a simplified homogeneous cylindrical human-equivalent phantom; not measured human exposure and not a blanket regulatory-compliance certification. Local reference-level exceedance is distinct from the underlying dosimetric assessment.
